items.title: Player interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2012
items.q: he played in Basie’s band and Hamp back then

ctx.x: Well do you have an opinion on why trad jazz and New Orleans jazz and that, it’s so hard to define the stuff, but it doesn’t seem to be taken as seriously as John Coltrane, or Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers. There seems to be —

Well I think, yeah, I think mainly right now the reason for that is because what’s promoted as — let’s see I’m trying to say this — the jazz that’s being taught at universities is more like bebop. And I don’t know that, and especially in America — I mean I think back to that whole value system for this music, be it whatever style of jazz, you just don’t have, our society doesn’t value it the way they did, I think, in the past, or as much, or maybe as many people, maybe that’s the better way to say it. And I think…

so I mean there was some appreciation in every home, there was some appreciation of music. I mean people appreciated it, even if they weren’t going to be professional musicians, most people maybe had experiences with starting in a band program, or they could at least have some basic understanding to what it would take to become on the level that we know some of our greatest professional musicians are. And so you did have some appreciation there. But now it’s just all sports it seems. And I’m not knocking the…
